headline: All majors below their 200-day lines with mixed momentum; whales pulling coins off exchanges while funding stays elevated and the crowd sits in fear.
paragraphs: The regime is unified and underwater. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have achieved a golden cross. The distance from the 12-month high tells the story of drawdown: Bitcoin sits 47.7% below its peak, Ethereum 60%, Solana 68.7%, and Doge 75.6%. This is not a rally in progress; it is a market that has gone through a major cycle and not yet reclaimed its recent highs. The one finding in trend structure is that Bitcoin and Solana both have MACD above the signal line while price remains below the 200-day, which is a mild divergence worth noting, not yet a reversal but a sign momentum is not falling apart beneath the surface.

Momentum itself is muted and patchy. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 56.3, right at the middle of the neutral range, with MACD positive but no thrust. Ethereum's RSI is 58.3 and MACD is actually below the signal line, suggesting momentum may be rolling over even as price ticked up 0.73% on the day. Cardano shows RSI at 67.1, technically in overbought territory, yet its 24-hour move was negative 0.58%, a clear divergence between the momentum gauge and price action on the day. Solana and BNB both carry elevated RSI in the upper 50s and low 60s, and both show MACD above signal, but none of this is translating into sustained rallies. XRP's RSI sits at 41.5, firmly in the lower half of the range, and its week saw a 3.69% decline. The pattern is a market where momentum is not yet compressed enough to signal capitulation, nor strong enough to signal conviction.

Derivatives positioning reveals crowding and elevation in funding costs. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding rate is 0.01% (annualized to 10.9%), which is not extreme but is a clear bid to hold longs. Open interest in Bitcoin on OKX stands at $2.09 billion with a long-to-short ratio of 1.14, meaning longs outnumber shorts but not by a dramatic margin. Ethereum shows a 1.33 ratio on $1.30 billion open interest, and here the funding is lower at 0.0042% 8-hour (annualizing to 4.7%), suggesting the long bias is less expensive to carry. Solana tells a different story: 2.01 long-to-short ratio on $245 million open interest with 0.0093% 8-hour funding (10.2% annualized), a crowded long setup. XRP and Doge show the most extreme skew: 3.61 and 4.99 long-to-short ratios respectively, both with 0.01% 8-hour funding (11% annualized). The liquidation window over the last 22 to 24 hours shows shorts being wiped out, especially in Ethereum (3.92 million in short liquidations), Solana (1.08 million shorts), and Doge (132k longs but only 16k shorts). This is the tape of a market where longs are concentrated, expensive to hold, and shorts are being squeezed; that is historically fragile positioning when momentum stalls.

Whale activity over the last 48 hours shows net Bitcoin movement of $103 million off exchanges, with the largest single move being $117.99 million leaving Kraken and another $50.07 million from the same venue. On the inflow side, Binance took in $65 million. Over the most recent full week, whale net flows have been volatile: negative $86.7 million, then positive $385.7 million, then sharply positive $1.075 billion, then back down to $67.2 million positive. The pattern is not a sustained directional move but oscillation, with one massive outflow week preceded and followed by inflows. Today's 48-hour outflow does not yet constitute a regime; it is a signal worth tracking. Stablecoin supply sits at $306.2 billion, down 1.03% over the last 30 days, meaning dry powder is being deployed or trickling out. Spot ETF flows into Bitcoin hit $101.7 million on 7 August alone, with five consecutive days of inflows totaling $865.3 million. Ethereum saw $49.6 million on the same day and $243.7 million over the last five sessions, though only four days show the same direction. These are steady but modest TradFi bids into the space.

Sentiment has compressed into fear at 31, sitting in the lower half of a 30-day range of 22 to 33. The crowd is genuinely nervous. Yet the tape shows mixed signals: ETF flows are positive and persistent (five days for Bitcoin, four for Ethereum), whales are pulling coins into cold storage on balance over the last two days, and funding, while elevated, is not stratospheric. This is the classic disconnect between emotional fear and actual capital behavior. When the crowd panics but institutions buy and whales hodl, the move often has room; when they misalign the other way, the market is vulnerable to a fast reversal. The 24-hour market cap change of 0.62% and Bitcoin's 0.46% move on the day are both tepid, which squares with the range-bound tape: momentum is not strong enough to break out, drawdown is not deep enough to trigger panic selling, and positioning is crowded enough to threaten a squeeze but not yet forced.

Watch for a reclaim of the 200-day line in Bitcoin or Ethereum, which would signal a structural shift from a bear regime to something more neutral. Monitor the long-to-short ratio and funding on Solana, XRP, and Doge for compression, because if those ratios fall and funding inverts to negative (shorts paying longs), the crowded long setup will have broken. Track whale flows over the next week: if the current outflow trend (off exchanges) persists for three more sessions alongside positive ETF inflows, that divergence between retail TradFi entry and whale hoarding is a potent signal. Finally, watch Cardano's RSI, which is genuinely overbought at 67 despite a negative day; if that fails to print a higher high, it signals momentum divergence is real and broadening.
